acceptance.assertion: A deterministic, versioned manifest-v2 root points to bounded child indexes and leaf shard descriptors instead of embedding the complete shard directory; every node carries exact counts, content digests, path/version binding and canonical ordering, and the 100k schema-realistic fixture stays within the contract root and node transfer budgets.

A versioned aggregate-v2 root exposes bounded, demand-loadable geographic and digital summary segments without embedding the complete 100k aggregate; segment membership, totals and digests reconcile exactly with the generated catalogue and shard hierarchy.

The catalogue runtime accepts the existing manifest-v1 and aggregate-v1 contract unchanged and supports manifest-v2 and aggregate-v2 through explicit version dispatch; search, map and digital navigation request only required hierarchy nodes and segments, reject unknown versions, and fail closed with bounded recovery when a node is missing, corrupt or digest-mismatched.

The current two-hex runtime and visible build-bound bootstrap remain the default delivery path. A machine-readable migration and rollback guard prevents v2 cutover or bootstrap removal until all deterministic, browser-budget and physical-device evidence gates are satisfied; this task does not claim the physical-device gate itself.

Schema-realistic deterministic 1k, 10k and 100k fixtures validate hierarchy integrity, old-manifest compatibility, rollback and exact transfer and request budgets. Public-browser tests prove demand-loaded search, map and digital flows on the exact implementation head without eager transfer of the complete manifest or aggregate.

Canonical generators, contracts, source runtime assets, generated public pages, immutable release output, architecture documentation and evidence files agree on one exact versioned hierarchy contract and are regenerated deterministically.

The exact published head passes focused JavaScript and Python tests, full repository validation, browser smoke, git diff checks, diff-bound self-review and all required GitHub checks; material review findings are resolved before merge. Runtime cutover, bootstrap removal and production deployment remain outside this task.

approval.note: The user explicitly requested implementation of the next Commonworld task through Grabowski on 2026-08-03. Work must use an isolated coordinated worktree and must not touch the foreign dirty canonical checkout.

goal: Introduce a versioned, backward-compatible hierarchical Commonworld catalogue manifest and aggregate contract that can use deeper SHA-256 shard prefixes without transferring a flat directory of thousands of descriptors, while preserving the current two-hex runtime and build-bound bootstrap until the new path is fully proven.

does_not_establish: permission to modify the foreign dirty canonical checkout or its lifecycle

title: Introduce a hierarchical catalogue manifest and aggregate before 100k scale
